messages:
maria: Quick help — opened a docs PR for the CLI evidence export playbook. I added an example showing exporting tenant-scoped audit logs but legal flagged the term 'tenant' and a couple of flags in the snippet. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3421. Can folks scan for CLI correctness + SOC2-safe wording before I merge?

docs-bot: PR created: maria/cli-evidence-playbook-update (#3421) — link above. CI: docs build pending.

raj: Looking now. One thing: the CLI example uses `--include-tenant` which isn't a real flag in the export tool. The current CLI uses `--scope` with values `account` or `customer`. Suggest changing to `--scope customer`. Also avoid using raw tenant IDs in examples.

raj: Suggested command (replace in the example):

```bash
redwoodctl export-evidence --scope customer --customer-id 12345 --output ./evidence.jsonl \\n  --start 2025-12-01 --end 2025-12-31
```

oliver: Security suggestion: prefer the term "customer" everywhere instead of tenant. Also don't state TTL as "retention TTL 90 days" — phrase as "retention window: 90 days" or "records retained for 90 days" to avoid implying automated deletion behavior without context. And add a short note about encryption in transit+at-rest.

tess: I can take the wording updates. Quick question for legal: the example currently says `--kms false` to show no customer-managed key; legal asked to always mention KMS option. Do we need to show both variants (default service key vs CMK) in the playbook?

legal-ops: SOC2-wise our guidance: avoid operational promises like "we delete after X" — prefer neutral phrasing like "records are retained for up to 90 days unless a longer retention is required by contract or legal hold." For KMS, show both examples and a one-line callout: "If you supply a customer-managed key, evidence will be encrypted with your CMK during export." Example sentence: "For exports using customer-managed keys (CMK), ensure your KMS key policy allows export operations."

raj: Also a tiny nit: the JSONL sample row includes `user.email` — redact any PII in top-level examples and use placeholders e.g. `user.email: "redacted@example.com"` or `user_id: "cust-123"` depending on what we want to illustrate.

maria: Good catches. Plan: I'll replace `--include-tenant` with `--scope customer`, swap phrasing to "records retained for up to 90 days", add a second CLI snippet showing `--kms-key arn:aws:kms:...` and update the sample JSONL to use placeholders. After I push, I'll tag @legal-ops for final sign-off.

legal-ops: Sound good — once the KMS example and neutral retention phrasing are in, we can sign off. :thumbsup:

oliver: Also add a one-liner about audit export access control: "Exports respect IAM and audit access policies; use least privilege for export roles."

maria: Will do — thanks all, pushing changes in a few mins and will ping once CI passes.

raj: Thanks — small follow-up: can we add a short note under Troubleshooting about the common error `export: unauthorized` and suggest verifying `redwoodctl` role bindings? One-liner is fine.

maria: Yep adding that now.

docs-bot: CI passed for PR #3421 — doc build OK.

maria: Updated and pushed. Tagging @legal-ops for sign-off.

legal-ops: Reviewed and approved. You can merge once the release checklist is green.

maria: Merged. Thanks everyone! :tada:
